inclusion_criteria.value: Any patient with acute respiratory failure of any cause who was mechanically ventilated according to the ARDS network guidelines with a prerequisite of high inspiratory driving pressure (plateau pressure of up to 25 to 30 cm H2O) and at least one of four severity criteria: (1) low total respiratory system compliance (CT), defined as less than 50 mL/cm H2O; (2) P/F ratio of less than 300 mmHg; (3) need for a PEEP greater than 10 cm H2O to maintain SaO2 of >90%; (4) PaCO2 over 60 mmHg or PH less than 7.2 attributed to respiratory acidosis. Eligibility criteria had to be met within 24 hours of ICU admission or within 24 hours from commencing mechanical ventilation.

provenance.quote: Eligibility criteria (Figure 1) for insertion of esophageal balloon included any patient with acute respiratory failure of any cause who was mechanically ventilated according to the ARDS network guidelines with a prerequisite of high inspiratory driving pressure (plateau pressure of up to 25 to 30 cm H2O) and at least one of the following four severity inclusion criteria

exclusion_criteria.value: known bronchial asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), previous lung or chest wall surgery, previous esophageal surgery, known achalasia or any other esophageal motility or spasm disorder, known or suspected esophageal varices, presence of chest thoracostomy tube that was inserted due to pneumothorax, and any significant chest wall abnormality such as kyphoscoliosis

provenance.quote: Patients with any of the following were excluded from the study: known bronchial asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), previous lung or chest wall surgery, previous esophageal surgery, known achalasia or any other esophageal motility or spasm disorder, known or suspected esophageal varices, presence of chest thoracostomy tube that was inserted due to pneumothorax, and any significant chest wall abnormality such as kyphoscoliosis.
ARDS was defined according to the Berlin definition [6].

provenance.quote: Patients were supine and were ventilated by a commercially available ventilator (Avea, CareFusion Inc., CA, USA). The ventilator is supplied with a built-in module allowing the connection of an esophageal balloon catheter for continuous transpulmonary pressure monitoring.

method_verbatim.value: For further confirmation of correct esophageal balloon positioning an "occlusion test" was performed. We have modified the original "occlusion test" [7] by inserting a thin pressure recording tracheal catheter capable of measuring pressure in air interface.

provenance.quote: For further confirmation of correct esophageal balloon positioning an "occlusion test" was performed. We have modified the original "occlusion test" [7] by inserting a thin pressure recording tracheal catheter capable of measuring pressure in air interface.

position_verification.value: Balloon first inserted into stomach to 60-70 cm from incisors, then slowly pooled caudally until heart beat noticed on esophageal pressure tracing; occlusion test with tracheal catheter

provenance.quote: The balloon was first inserted into the stomach to a depth of 60 to 70 cm from the incisors. Thereafter, it was slowly pooled caudally until heart beat could be noticed on the esophageal pressure tracing.

occlusion_ratio_acceptance.value: esophageal and tracheal pressures during an inspiratory effort against an occluded airway were within 10% of each other

provenance.quote: A correct esophageal balloon position was considered appropriate if the values of esophageal and tracheal pressures during an inspiratory effort against an occluded airway were within 10% of each other.

method_verbatim.value: Transpulmonary pressures computed from airway and esophageal pressures; no offset subtraction applied

provenance.quote: For these reasons and for the sake of simplicity we chose not to subtract from the measured esophageal value.

pes_correction_applied.value: none; authors explicitly chose not to subtract the mediastinal-weight offset

strategy_verbatim.value: PEEP was adjusted according to end expiratory transpulmonary (EETP) pressure, with the aim of keeping EETP pressure close to zero or slightly positive, while achieving oxygenation target of PaO2 of 60 to 90 mmHg, or oxygen saturation of 88 to 95%; inspiratory driving pressure was adjusted according to end inspiratory transpulmonary (EITP) pressure, with the aim of achieving a tidal volume of 6-8 mL/kg (IBW), while at the same time not exceeding EITP pressure of 25 cm H2O.

subgroup_flags.classification_notes: ards_only: all six patients had ARDS by Berlin definition. obesity_subgroup unclear: no BMI reported. timing early_within_48h: eligibility and balloon insertion within 24 hours of ICU admission or commencing mechanical ventilation. ptp_target_subgroups: EETP target 'close to zero or slightly positive' coded as absolute_zero_end_expiratory_ptp; the EITP ceiling of 25 cmH2O is a safety limit rather than a titration target and has no matching enum value. Mortality ranking: 28-day is the only mortality timepoint reported, so it is the longest.

extraction_flags.overlap_evidence: No overlap with any other report in the review pool. Registration NCT01668368 is a larger ongoing study at Wolfson Medical Center, Holon, Israel; no other record in COHORTS.md shares this registration, centre, or enrolment window. The six patients are described as consecutive at this single centre.
unclear_items: adults_18_plus: no explicit age criterion stated; coded yes from adult ICU setting and patient ages 40-84 in Table 1

eligibility.criteria.balloon_guided_peep_titration: COHORTS.md flags this study as sitting at the case-series boundary (n=6 uncontrolled before/after); it meets n>=5 and the balloon did change ventilator settings, so coded yes

intervention.peep_titration_target.strategy: target is 'close to zero or slightly positive' EETP, ambiguous between zero and slightly positive; coded combined_end_expiratory_and_end_inspiratory with the EITP 25 cmH2O ceiling
population.age / sex_female / sex_male: only per-patient values in Table 1 (49/F, 67/M, 84/F, 76/M, 40/F, 81/M); cohort-level summary not reported and not derived
outcomes PaCO2 baseline mean 108.33 vs Table 1 individual values 141, 96, 99, 93, 140, 81 (mean 108.33 consistent); Table 2 PaCO2 'After' values are individual, not the 1-hour group mean
feasibility.n_measurement_not_obtainable: not reported whether any measurement attempt failed while placement succeeded
design.enrolment_start/end: not reported; patients enrolled in a larger ongoing study (NCT01668368) with no dates given
extraction_flags.general_notes: Case cohort of 6 consecutive patients, substudy of a larger registered study (NCT01668368). Table 2 reports individual before/after values per patient (PEEP, inspiratory driving pressure, plateau, EITP, EETP, tidal volume/IBW, PaCO2, cardiac index); Table 3 reports group means at baseline and 1 hour. Statistical significance threshold P<=0.01 due to small sample. Chest wall compliance SDs (63.5 and 124) are as printed and appear implausibly large relative to the mean. Cause of death in all four nonsurvivors was sepsis with multiorgan failure.
